name: CASE
desc: Covers the CASE function: ordered match-context conditions, lazy value-context results and else branches, implicit FAIL when no condition matches, arbitrary returned values, partial/exact structural patterns, dynamic failure trapping, lexical namespaces and captures, independent results, metadata, dates, errors, and resources. LOCAL examples rebind NODE to a discriminator so CASE can use direct scalar/object patterns, while retaining original data in TEMP for selected results. FAIL has its own collection.

tests.name: Selection and returned values
tests.desc: One or more condition/result pairs are required. The first matching condition selects its result, and no-else forms use implied FAIL when all conditions fail. Selected values support all JSON types without truthiness-based fallback.

tests.name: Selected result is an evaluated expression
Match-context conditions
tests.desc: Plain scalars compare against NODE rather than being tested for truthiness. Objects and escaped arrays imply HAS; explicit IS can require exact structure. Match expressions act as predicates, while reference/function conditions return literal values to match.

Lazy evaluation and failure boundaries
tests.desc: Only conditions up to the first match and the selected result are evaluated. FAIL, missing references, and invalid runtime operands in conditions count as non-matches. A selected result error propagates instead of trying later branches or the else. Valid but unreachable failures are never evaluated.

LOCAL convenience and restoration
tests.desc: LOCAL can save the original record, rebind NODE to a nested discriminator, and let CASE use direct patterns. All conditions and the selected result see that lexical scope. Nested branch-local bindings restore the caller after their result is computed.

Namespaces, constructed results, and metadata
tests.desc: CASE uses invocation-time CONST/STASH/TEMP/common-expression bindings. Its conditions do not publish captures to CAP; outer captures remain available. Selected references are returned as independent constructed values and preserve array SPLIT metadata.

Syntax, fatal errors, and resource limits
tests.desc: CASE requires at least one condition/result pair. Syntax errors in reached expressions remain INVALID_GRAFT. RESOURCE_LIMIT and UNSUPPORTED_GRAFT in reached conditions or results are fatal rather than causing fall-through. Missing else always uses explicit FAIL semantics, never a static INVALID_GRAFT upgrade.
